notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main, so there was no candidate id to create from. The schema follows the arm9/dCcAc_c and arm9/Clipper entries, which took the same route.

dExtBlendAnmModel_c is the dExtAnmModel_c child that blends from the previous pose into a new BCA_File animation: SetAnim arms the blend (fast path re-flags in place when the file is unchanged), Advance ramps blendWeight toward 1.0, and Virtual10/UpdateVerts route through the blending helper func_0204531c below 1.0 and through the unblended dExtSimpleModel_c paths at it.

The fold takes the method run and the lifecycle tail D0, D1, C1 (0x02016644..0x02016714). ~dExtBlendAnmModel_c() is the key function. RTTI is off so the dExtBlendAnmModel_c records are not emitted. D2 and C2 are homeless and deadstripped. The _ZThn80_ thunks at 0x02017168..0x020171c8 are enrolled in src/engine/model/ModelAnimThunks.cpp; this TU's copies are deadstrip-duplicates. _ZTV19dExtBlendAnmModel_c is deadstrip-data: the secondary preamble's RTTI-off zeros are masked, the slots match, and the retail vtable is unchanged.

func_020165c4 folds in as an extern "C" function (the ROM does not record its linkage; DoSetFile is its only caller in the tree): include/dExtBlendAnmModel_c.h documents it as DoSetFile's tail (it allocates the unk_6c blend buffer the destructor frees). It keeps its address label rather than gaining an invented member name; the only caller is DoSetFile in this same TU.

SetAnim stays a mangled extern "C" definition (wall 6az, notes/mwccarm-codegen.md): the Fix12<int> by-value parameter keeps the free spelling, and its call to dExtFrameCtrl_c::SetAnimation keeps the mangled spelling too because passing the real declaration's Fix12<int> by value homes the argument to the caller's stack. SetFlags takes a plain int and is spelled as the member call it is; the Animation subobject pointer comes from &static_cast<Animation &>(*thiz), the reference form that emits the bare add rather than the null-checked this adjustment a pointer static_cast produces.

The file is written ROM-descending because mwccarm emits .text in reverse source order under default deferred codegen. The constructor and destructor are first in the source so their clusters land after the methods: D2, D0, D1, the thunks, then C1, C2. Deadstripping D2, C2 and the thunks leaves D0, D1, C1 in cartridge order, 0x020163e0..0x02016714.
